name: Hinting — The Sweet Ache of Anticipation
summary: Hinting builds pleasure through sustained, irregular teasing: repeatedly approaching sensitive areas without fully indulging them—like driving past a house without knocking yet. Playful fake-outs keep anticipation high across the session instead of rushing to climax, so the eventual release is bigger.
detailed_description: The core principle is less direct contact plus many near-touches, which builds a larger eventual release than immediate gratification. Hinting works best as a warmup and throughout play, not just at the start. OMGYES describes three targets—the whole area, the opening, and the clitoris—plus fine-tuning rules: keep touch light, stay irregular and unpredictable, repeat enough sets to build, give it several minutes, and don't over-tease with constant near-misses. Slow each near-miss stroke so the 'almost' lingers.
stepwise_structure: 1. Begin during warmup, before direct clitoral contact or penetration.
2. Approach a sensitive target, then veer away at the last moment—repeat as playful fake-outs.
3. Keep pressure light; hinting depends on teasing, not force.
4. Stay irregular—avoid predictable patterns like grazing on every third pass.
5. Repeat over many sets across several minutes; a few hints alone won't build much.
6. Space out the near-misses; too many 'almost' touches cause habituation.
7. Slow each near-miss stroke so the anticipation lingers.
safety_notes: Excessive teasing can tip into frustration—read feedback and indulge when it's wanted.
Light touch only; heavy pressing defeats the purpose and can desensitize.
Adults in consensual contexts only; not a substitute for professional care.

fine_tuning.repetition: Repeat hinting many times; a few sets rarely build noticeable anticipation.
fine_tuning.light_touch: Less pressure is better—heavy pressing defeats the teasing effect.
fine_tuning.get_irregular: Avoid predictable patterns (e.g. grazing on every third pass); unpredictability keeps it fresh.
fine_tuning.not_too_brief: Allow several minutes for anticipation to build.
fine_tuning.not_too_often: Use fewer 'almost' touches; space out near-misses to avoid habituation.
fine_tuning.elongate_the_almost: Slow the stroke so each near-miss lingers rather than being a quick dismissal.
